newsitem.title: UK: Pilkington edges higher after results.
newsitem.headline: Pilkington edges higher after results.

text.p: Shares in British glassmaker Pilkington Plc edged higher in early trading despite reporting a fall in profits in the six months to September 30.

Profit before tax was 75 million stg after an exceptional charge of seven million stg on the sale of the Barnes-Hind contact lens business. Profits were down from 104 million stg in the same period last year.
But the fall had been anticipated and an upbeat statement helped lift the shares 3p to 172-1/2p at the open.
"The results were ahead of my expectations and the statement was pretty bullish," said one analyst.

"The negative comnments on Europe were expected and it seems to be turning...things seem to be firming up and the outlook looks good." Interim results were affetcted by significant price falls in Europe, said Pilkington chairman Nigel Rudd, but toward the end of September and during October prices and volumes picked up.
Businesses elsewhere, particularly in North and South America continue to perform well, he said, adding that he expected to see an improving trend in the second half of the year.
The company said it's underlying strategy remains to emphasise new product development, increase downstream processing, cost reduction and cash generation.
